pros4-actions-001:actions-04.rationale: Indonesian news uses terpeleset in the body and tergelincir in the headline for the same slipping event; the proposed national preference is nonexclusive.

sources.observation: The same bathroom-safety article uses tergelincir in its title and terpeleset in its text.
sources.sense: lose footing on a slippery surface

pros4-actions-001:actions-05.rationale: A current Malaysian lifestyle article uses menjemur and menyidai together for drying laundry; menyidai is natural but the exclusive preference contrast needs review.

sources.observation: The article calls the activity menjemur or menyidai pakaian and uses menyidai repeatedly.
sources.sense: hang washed clothes outdoors to dry

pros4-actions-001:actions-07.rationale: A Malaysian municipal rule uses mengepam tandas, but current commercial service language also uses flush tandas; everyday exclusivity is unclear.

sources.observation: Municipal public-toilet rules instruct users to mengepam after use.
A plumbing service advertises repair of a flush tandas.

pros4-food-001:food-08.rationale: Malaysian retail uses penapis makanan for the utensil; no observed source suggests a misleading everyday claim, though preference was not measured.

sources.observation: Malaysian marketplace product category and listings use penapis makanan.
sources.sense: utensil for separating solids from liquid

pros4-food-001:food-09.rationale: Both gelas ukur and gelas takar denote the tool in Indonesian retail usage, while Malaysian cooking sources use cawan penyukat. The alternative is nonblocking.

sources.observation: Retailer describes gelas takar as also called gelas ukur.
Cooking equipment supplier includes cawan penyukat in its equipment list.

pros4-food-001:food-10.rationale: A Malaysian appliance retailer markets one item as both pengisar and blender. The localized form is genuinely product-facing, but borrowing competition merits audit.

sources.observation: A single appliance product title contains both Pengisar and Power Blender.

pros4-health-001:health-02.rationale: A Malaysian university health programme uses cergas for physical fitness; an English programme title uses fit but does not displace the Malay adjective.

sources.observation: University health programme aims to make participants cergas dan sihat.

pros4-health-001:health-03.rationale: The authoritative entry confirms pekak and relates it to tuli, but dictionary inclusion does not establish an everyday national preference.

sources.observation: DBP entry gives the meaning of pekak and lists tuli as a related form.

pros4-health-001:health-10.rationale: Malaysian health language uses menopaus alongside putus haid; proposed contrast is plausible but not an exclusive everyday preference.

sources.observation: University care text relates menopaus and putus haid in the same clinical discussion.

pros4-home-001:home-04.rationale: Indonesian current publication uses kantong for a jeans pocket; this competes with saku in the same clothing sense.

sources.observation: National radio article calls the small jeans pocket a kantong kecil.

pros4-home-001:home-06.rationale: Malaysian mainstream retail reporting repeatedly uses jenama for a commercial product brand; English house brand appears as a borrowing in context.

sources.observation: Retail article uses jenama throughout while explaining house brand.

pros4-home-001:home-09.rationale: An Indonesian bank uses cicilan for purchases but also angsuran for scheduled payments, showing same-market competition rather than a settled exclusive preference.

sources.observation: Bank consumer guidance uses Cicilan for its product and angsuran for the monthly payment.
sources.sense: one of several scheduled payments for a purchase

pros4-home-001:home-10.rationale: A Malaysian marketplace help page uses pemulangan wang and bayaran balik for the same refund process; everyday distinction is nonexclusive.

sources.observation: Marketplace help uses pemulangan wang for processing and pulangan/bayaran balik for requests.
sources.sense: money returned after a purchase is cancelled or returned

pros4-technology-001:technology-03.rationale: A Malaysian university repository treats penyelidikan and kajian as related academic activity; the proposed preference needs audit rather than automatic rejection.

sources.observation: Academic repository summary mentions both penyelidikan and kajian akademik.
sources.sense: systematic study to discover or establish facts

pros4-technology-001:technology-08.rationale: Malaysian app support uses both notifikasi and pemberitahuan for a push alert. Both are product-facing; the contrast may overstate preference.

sources.observation: Help article title uses Notifikasi and pemberitahuan to name the same app alert.
sources.sense: message alert from an application or service

pros4-technology-001:technology-09.rationale: Malaysian government guidance uses resume and CV interchangeably in job applications; Indonesian riwayat hidup may be broader, so cue and preference merit audit.

sources.sense: document summarizing a person's education and work history
